speaker: antlered
text: somebody tell them about me.
spokenText: somebody tell them about me.

speaker: brock
text: "This deep, the maps stop helping. This deep, Camp Hearthwood stops being the last camp on the ridge and starts being the last camp, period."
spokenText: This deep, the maps stop helping. This deep, Camp Hearthwood stops being the last camp on the ridge and starts being the last camp, period.

speaker: brock
text: "Bring back whatever you find. I am done being surprised at my age. I would just like to be informed."
spokenText: Bring back whatever you find. I am done being surprised at my age. I would just like to be informed.

speaker: brock
text: "You are past the treeline proper now. Further than I go. Further than most of my old troop got." A pause. "Different makers stamp those tokens out there. Different hands, different tin. They compete. I do not know for what."
spokenText: You are past the treeline proper now. Further than I go. Further than most of my old troop got. Different makers stamp those tokens out there. Different hands, different tin. They compete. I do not know for what.

speaker: brock
text: "Bring me one, if you can pry it loose. I have wanted to look at one up close for thirty years. I have also, and I cannot stress this enough, been too much of a coward."
spokenText: Bring me one, if you can pry it loose. I have wanted to look at one up close for thirty years. I have also, and I cannot stress this enough, been too much of a coward.

speaker: brock
text: "BRAMBLEBUCK, down. First one Signed, if the old stories are even true, which means you just beat the one with seniority."
spokenText: BRAMBLEBUCK, down. First one Signed, if the old stories are even true, which means you just beat the one with seniority.

speaker: brock
text: "Do not let it go to your head. It was, and I want to stress this, a rabbit."
spokenText: Do not let it go to your head. It was, and I want to stress this, a rabbit.

speaker: brock
text: "OLD NOBODY. HOLLOWANTLER, if you want its whole name, though nothing out there wants to hear it said twice. Down. Thirty years running this camp did not prepare me for how quiet that would be."
spokenText: OLD NOBODY. HOLLOWANTLER, if you want its whole name, though nothing out there wants to hear it said twice. Down. Thirty years running this camp did not prepare me for how quiet that would be.

speaker: brock
text: "I had a whole speech ready. I am not giving it tonight. Go celebrate. And do not ask me about the twelfth name yet. Some other night."
spokenText: I had a whole speech ready. I am not giving it tonight. Go celebrate. And do not ask me about the twelfth name yet. Some other night.

speaker: brock
text: "You saw a whole dawn out there and came back to tell me about it. Sit by the fire. The actual seat, not the log with the splinter."
spokenText: You saw a whole dawn out there and came back to tell me about it. Sit by the fire. The actual seat, not the log with the splinter.

speaker: brock
text: "Thirty years I ran this camp on the theory that somebody eventually would. Thank you for proving the theory. Cocoa is on me tonight."
spokenText: Thirty years I ran this camp on the theory that somebody eventually would. Thank you for proving the theory. Cocoa is on me tonight.

speaker: brock
text: "Back already." Brock does not look up from the fire. "Good. That means you are still breathing. Sit. I only tell this story once, and I am not repeating the good parts."
spokenText: Back already. Good. That means you are still breathing. Sit. I only tell this story once, and I am not repeating the good parts.

speaker: brock
text: "Thirty years ago I brought twelve kids up this ridge. I brought one down. That is a fireside talk for later. Tonight, go get badges."
spokenText: Thirty years ago I brought twelve kids up this ridge. I brought one down. That is a fireside talk for later. Tonight, go get badges.

speaker: brock
text: "You are keeping notes. Good. Nobody who ever camped this ridge before you wrote a single thing down, and look how that went."
spokenText: You are keeping notes. Good. Nobody who ever camped this ridge before you wrote a single thing down, and look how that went.

speaker: brock
text: "Keep the journal. I will read it when you are done needing it. Preferably a long time from now."
spokenText: Keep the journal. I will read it when you are done needing it. Preferably a long time from now.

speaker: brock
text: "Five times back to this fire in a body bag, more or less. I stopped flinching around number three. Professional courtesy."
spokenText: Five times back to this fire in a body bag, more or less. I stopped flinching around number three. Professional courtesy.

speaker: brock
text: "You keep coming back, though. That is either grit or a badge quota you are very committed to. I am choosing to believe grit."
spokenText: You keep coming back, though. That is either grit or a badge quota you are very committed to. I am choosing to believe grit.

speaker: brock
text: "That journal of yours is getting thick. You have written down more about this ridge than I managed in thirty years, and I LIVE here."
spokenText: That journal of yours is getting thick. You have written down more about this ridge than I managed in thirty years, and I LIVE here.

speaker: brock
text: "Feel free to be smug about it. Once."
spokenText: Feel free to be smug about it. Once.

speaker: brock
text: "THE TALLYMAN, finally handled. He has been walking off with badges since before you were born. Did you get any of them back?"
spokenText: THE TALLYMAN, finally handled. He has been walking off with badges since before you were born. Did you get any of them back?

speaker: brock
text: "No? Of course not. He is very organized about it. There is probably a ledger."
spokenText: No? Of course not. He is very organized about it. There is probably a ledger.

speaker: brock
text: "Three of the named ones, put down for good. That is not luck, kid. That is a pattern. I am almost proud, which is new for me."
spokenText: Three of the named ones, put down for good. That is not luck, kid. That is a pattern. I am almost proud, which is new for me.

speaker: brock
text: "Try not to let it go to your head twice in one season."
spokenText: Try not to let it go to your head twice in one season.

speaker: brock
text: "You have gotten a good look at two of them now. Notice the tin? Every marked critter wears one, pressed right into the fur. Somebody out there is stamping those by hand."
spokenText: You have gotten a good look at two of them now. Notice the tin? Every marked critter wears one, pressed right into the fur. Somebody out there is stamping those by hand.

speaker: brock
text: "Do not ask me who. I have theories. None of them let me sleep."
spokenText: Do not ask me who. I have theories. None of them let me sleep.

speaker: brock
text: "You saw the dawn. Thirty years I have run this camp and I can count dawn-watchers on one paw." He salutes with the coffee.
spokenText: You saw the dawn. Thirty years I have run this camp and I can count dawn-watchers on one paw.

speaker: brock
text: "OLD NOBODY is down and the sun came up. Do not get comfortable. Antlers grow back, and so, probably, does he."
spokenText: OLD NOBODY is down and the sun came up. Do not get comfortable. Antlers grow back, and so, probably, does he.

speaker: brock
text: "OLD NOBODY. HOLLOWANTLER, if you want its whole name, though nobody out there wants to be caught saying it twice. You got further than most of Troop 12 ever did. Again."
spokenText: OLD NOBODY. HOLLOWANTLER, if you want its whole name, though nobody out there wants to be caught saying it twice. You got further than most of Troop 12 ever did. Again.

speaker: brock
text: "Bats. Hate the wobble. Everyone hates the wobble."
spokenText: Bats. Hate the wobble. Everyone hates the wobble.

speaker: brock
text: "A beaver. Death by municipal engineering. There is a badge for irony somewhere."
spokenText: A beaver. Death by municipal engineering. There is a badge for irony somewhere.

speaker: brock
text: "Boars telegraph the charge. Big exclamation of intent. Step LEFT, {scout}."
spokenText: Boars telegraph the charge. Big exclamation of intent. Step LEFT, {scout}.

speaker: brock
text: "Killed by a doe. Gentle eyes, they said. Nature is healing, they said."
spokenText: Killed by a doe. Gentle eyes, they said. Nature is healing, they said.

speaker: brock
text: "Foxes weave. Stop shooting where they were and shoot where they are going."
spokenText: Foxes weave. Stop shooting where they were and shoot where they are going.

speaker: brock
text: "Back again, {scout}. The forest keeps score, and so do I. Spend some badges before you go back out."
spokenText: Back again, {scout}. The forest keeps score, and so do I. Spend some badges before you go back out.

speaker: brock
text: "BRAMBLEBUCK. Signed young, they say, back when the tokens were still hand stamped. Every third landing it sprays. Count the hops, kid."
spokenText: BRAMBLEBUCK. Signed young, they say, back when the tokens were still hand stamped. Every third landing it sprays. Count the hops, kid.

speaker: brock
text: "The owls spit feathers. Keep your feet moving and they cannot lead the shot."
spokenText: The owls spit feathers. Keep your feet moving and they cannot lead the shot.

speaker: brock
text: "A rabbit got you. They hop, {scout}. You can see the whole attack coming from the air."
spokenText: A rabbit got you. They hop, {scout}. You can see the whole attack coming from the air.

speaker: brock
text: "A raccoon. It probably went through your pack afterwards. They always do."
spokenText: A raccoon. It probably went through your pack afterwards. They always do.

speaker: brock
text: "A squirrel. You were bested by a SQUIRREL. I have led this troop thirty years and it does not get less embarrassing."
spokenText: A squirrel. You were bested by a SQUIRREL. I have led this troop thirty years and it does not get less embarrassing.

speaker: brock
text: "THE TALLYMAN got you. Everything you own, he considers a loan. Stay off his rings and mind the raccoons he calls."
spokenText: THE TALLYMAN got you. Everything you own, he considers a loan. Stay off his rings and mind the raccoons he calls.

speaker: brock
text: "The Badge Board takes badges, not promises."
spokenText: The Badge Board takes badges, not promises.

speaker: brock
text: "Cocoa heals. That is not camp wisdom, that is medical fact out here."
spokenText: Cocoa heals. That is not camp wisdom, that is medical fact out here.

speaker: brock
text: "Hold your ground near the fire all you want. Out there, keep moving."
spokenText: Hold your ground near the fire all you want. Out there, keep moving.

speaker: brock
text: "Elites glow red. Chests fall out of them. Draw your own conclusions."
spokenText: Elites glow red. Chests fall out of them. Draw your own conclusions.

speaker: brock
text: "I knew that stag when he was a fawn. Before he got Signed. Shame. Great rack, though."
spokenText: I knew that stag when he was a fawn. Before he got Signed. Shame. Great rack, though.

speaker: brock
text: "Second Wind is not a myth. It is a purchase."
spokenText: Second Wind is not a myth. It is a purchase.

speaker: brock
text: "You aim with your eyes, not your feet. Strafe, {scout}. Strafe."
spokenText: You aim with your eyes, not your feet. Strafe, {scout}. Strafe.

speaker: brock
text: Scoutmaster Brock pokes the fire. "New blood. Good. Every critter out here that has truly seen one of them believes forever after, and belief like that leaves a mark, a little tin stamp pressed into the fur. We call that getting Signed. Earn badges. Come back alive. In that order, preferably."
spokenText: New blood. Good. Every critter out here that has truly seen one of them believes forever after, and belief like that leaves a mark, a little tin stamp pressed into the fur. We call that getting Signed. Earn badges. Come back alive. In that order, preferably.

speaker: brock
text: "Rules of Camp Hearthwood: respect the fire, bank your badges, and if a rabbit smiles at you, it already believes in something you really do not want it to."
spokenText: Rules of Camp Hearthwood: respect the fire, bank your badges, and if a rabbit smiles at you, it already believes in something you really do not want it to.

speaker: gus
text: That is a lot of critter.
spokenText: That is a lot of critter.

speaker: gus
text: You look like you skip breakfast.
spokenText: You look like you skip breakfast.

speaker: gus
text: I have a skillet with your name on it.
spokenText: I have a skillet with your name on it.

speaker: gus
text: Oh, this one has a whole legend. Fancy.
spokenText: Oh, this one has a whole legend. Fancy.

speaker: gus
text: Big name, big target.
spokenText: Big name, big target.

speaker: gus
text: I have been hungrier than this. Barely.
spokenText: I have been hungrier than this. Barely.

speaker: gus
text: OLD NOBODY. I have skipped fewer meals than you have skipped centuries.
spokenText: OLD NOBODY. I have skipped fewer meals than you have skipped centuries.

speaker: gus
text: The hopping one. I have heard the stories. Underwhelming so far.
spokenText: The hopping one. I have heard the stories. Underwhelming so far.

text: You are not getting my snacks. Try the badges instead.
spokenText: You are not getting my snacks. Try the badges instead.

speaker: gus
text: Ooh. Heavier than it looks.
spokenText: Ooh. Heavier than it looks.

speaker: gus
text: Is there food in this one?
spokenText: Is there food in this one?

speaker: gus
text: Someone... eat my rations...
spokenText: Someone... eat my rations...

speaker: gus
text: Do not let this go to waste... any of it...
spokenText: Do not let this go to waste... any of it...

speaker: gus
text: Tell them I finished my snacks first...
spokenText: Tell them I finished my snacks first...

speaker: gus
text: Worth it. The snacks were worth it...
spokenText: Worth it. The snacks were worth it...

speaker: gus
text: Nap time... forever, I guess...
spokenText: Nap time... forever, I guess...

text: I count them like sheep.
spokenText: I count them like sheep.

text: A hundred down. Arms are noodles.
spokenText: A hundred down. Arms are noodles.

text: I have been hit in the snacks.
spokenText: I have been hit in the snacks.

text: Everything hurts. Even the trail mix.
spokenText: Everything hurts. Even the trail mix.

speaker: gus
text: Walk it off. Walk it off.
spokenText: Walk it off. Walk it off.

speaker: gus
text: That woke me up, at least.
spokenText: That woke me up, at least.

speaker: gus
text: I am fine. The trail mix is not.
spokenText: I am fine. The trail mix is not.

speaker: gus
text: Rude. Very rude.
spokenText: Rude. Very rude.

speaker: gus
text: Nap is over.
spokenText: Nap is over.

speaker: gus
text: You woke me up. Rude.
spokenText: You woke me up. Rude.

speaker: gus
text: I brought snacks for after.
spokenText: I brought snacks for after.

speaker: gus
text: Big night. Bigger appetite.
spokenText: Big night. Bigger appetite.

speaker: gus
text: Gus is here. Relax, everybody.
spokenText: Gus is here. Relax, everybody.

speaker: gus
text: Whatever it believes in, I believe in lunch.
spokenText: Whatever it believes in, I believe in lunch.

speaker: gus
text: Let us get this over with, I am hungry.
spokenText: Let us get this over with, I am hungry.

speaker: gus
text: Slow and steady. Mostly slow.
spokenText: Slow and steady. Mostly slow.

speaker: gus
text: Gus stands, dusting crumbs. "Fine. But we eat after."
spokenText: Fine. But we eat after.

speaker: gus
text: Dawn already? Time for pancakes.
spokenText: Dawn already? Time for pancakes.

speaker: gus
text: We survived. Who wants eggs?
spokenText: We survived. Who wants eggs?

spokenText: hold still. it is only a pin.

spokenText: BRAMBLEBUCK! I have wanted to meet you since orientation!
